rationale:
The reviewed test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.additional_languages`.

- **Explicit language, regardless of extension.** Both constructors are called with a custom language and the misleading filename `misleading.rs`. `from_source_with` gets the text directly. `from_path_with` reads a real temporary file with that name. Both results must report `language() == "custom"`. They must also show the custom outline (`items[0].span == Span(0,9)`), the custom `structural_hash`, and the custom fingerprint value `"a  z"`. A constructor that picked a language from the `.rs` extension would fail these assertions.
- **Root contents returned.** `root.id().selector == ""`, and `root.text()` is the full source text. Both are asserted for the loaded and the supplied value.
- **Retains the language's fingerprinting rules** (via the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`). The test asserts `fingerprint().scheme == "custom-v2:own-v1"`. It drops the language and its configuration `Arc`, then asserts `fingerprint_scheme() == "custom-v2"`, so the value holds its own copy of the scheme. A selected child keeps the custom scheme, and its fingerprint equals the one from the path-loaded value. A second language with scheme `custom-v3` gives the same `structural_hash` but a different fingerprint, so the scheme is part of the retained rules.

The requirement states no error cases or other input classes. The test is also marked with a `{test}` reference to the subject.

text: The caller can supply an `OutlineLang` explicitly when loading a file or
outlining supplied text. These constructors use that language regardless of
the filename's extension and return root contents. The value retains that
An `OutlineContent` retains the source text, outline, and selected language's
fingerprinting scheme describing that same snapshot. Its item spans, selected
text, and structural hashes are derived from those bytes. A cached value keeps
these parts together; later file edits do not change the loaded value.
